analysis:
Examined three provider-swift engine bridge changes: EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Accounting.swift and EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift. All are local first-token deadline admission and performance-measurement logic. None touches the TB-002 wire contract, encryption, App Attest authorization, key custody, prefix-cache storage, the fan helper, or token and secret handling. No new network, file or trust-boundary surface was found.

1. EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift: Rate.observe now takes explicit restart and keepsNewest parameters. `at` becomes max(at, now) when the flag is set, so freshness follows the newest observation when completed work arrives out of order. The flag is gated by DeadlineAdmissionFixes.enabled. New helpers coversObservation and observationAge are read-only. The qualified-rate posture epoch logic is unchanged.

2. EngineV2Bridge+Accounting.swift: updateDecodeTpsEwma additionally smooths a CBv2DecodeRateShape. The shape is validated with isValid and falls back to batchRows 1, and non-finite tps is still rejected. The change is arithmetic only.

3. EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift: when admissionFixes is on and the engine has no recovery retirement, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve can substitute a calibrated anchor rate for the observed prefill rate. This can only relax admission after a contended sample when the engine is idle, the evidence is aged, and the posture is nominal. The impact is first-token deadline and availability behavior, not a confidentiality or authorization effect. The absolute deadline, physical capacity and retirement still apply. The resolve function and the decodeRateShape helper were not supplied, so I could not verify their bounds, for example that the anchor cannot be an unvetted or fabricated rate.

Remaining questions for integration: the implementation of IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve and DeadlineAdmissionFixes, and how the engine SDK consumes decodeRateShape. None of this has a visible confidentiality or integrity impact, so no threat IDs apply and I report no findings.
